---

## What Penny Is

**Penny** is an AI-powered revenue variance analyzer built for a professional services firm (Improving). It compares monthly revenue forecasts against actuals, identifies variances by customer and worker, and uses a Claude-powered agent to investigate root causes — explaining *why* revenue missed or exceeded forecast, not just *that* it did.

**Primary users:**
- **Finance (Richard's team):** Needs rollup visibility across all enterprises, variance categorization, and exportable reports — currently doing this manually in Power BI.
- **Presidents (office leads):** Need per-account explanations of every variance, every month — currently only get notified when variance exceeds 3% negative.

**The problem it replaces:** Manual screenshot-and-text communication from Finance to presidents, ad-hoc emails, no systematic categorization, and zero trend tracking across months.

---

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Frontend | React 18, TypeScript (strict), Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Zustand |
| Backend | Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy (async), Alembic |
| AI Layer | Anthropic Claude via `anthropic` SDK — streaming API with `tool_use`, multi-turn, up to 5 concurrent investigations |
| Database | SQLite (dev), Postgres-compatible via SQLAlchemy |
| Auth | Microsoft Entra ID (MSAL), RBAC at company/country/enterprise scope |
| Infra | Docker Compose (3 services: db, backend, frontend), Azure DevOps CI pipeline, nginx for frontend |
| Excel parsing | openpyxl (`data_only=True`), fuzzy name matching via difflib |
| Realtime | WebSocket streaming — agent text deltas and tool call results to the browser live |
| Testing | pytest (backend), Playwright E2E with Page Object Model (frontend) |

---

## What's Fully Built

**Data ingestion pipeline:**
- Parses 3 Excel workbook formats from Workday: forecast (resource planner), revenue actuals, and timesheet (time-and-time-off report)
- Fuzzy customer name resolution against a Client Name Mapping sheet
- Enterprise alias system — maps Workday entity names (e.g., "Winnipeg US" + "Winnipeg CA") to a single Penny enterprise
- Multi-file-set support (multiple forecast files merged per analysis run)

**Analysis engine:**
- Aggregator normalizes and joins forecast vs. actuals at the customer level
- Variance detector identifies mismatches with dollar and percent amounts
- Hours variance tracking alongside revenue variance
- Duplicate allocation detector (pre-investigation pass, runs before Claude)
- Mismatch detector (fuzzy name resolution failures)
- At-risk detector and flash projector (hours-only mode)
- 11+ variance categories seeded in the DB (over_allocation, wrong dates, rate mismatch, pipeline hours, etc.) with manual override UI

**Claude agent layer:**
- `per_variance_investigator.py` — one focused Claude API call per customer variance record, up to 5 concurrent (semaphore-bounded)
- `orchestrator.py` — coordinates all per-variance investigations, collects findings, runs post-processing
- `post_processor.py` — extracts structured `IssueFinding` records from LLM output, maps to categories, builds customer and person summaries
- `chat_tools.py` / `chat_tool_handlers.py` — separate conversational agent (chat mode) with tool_use for ad-hoc data queries
- `data_gatherer.py` — pre-fetches all relevant data for a variance record before the Claude call (context packing)
- Knowledge graph: `KGNode` and `KGEdge` tables built per analysis run — represents relationships between workers, customers, projects for agent context

**Frontend — fully built screens:**
- Login (Entra SSO)
- Company, Country, and Enterprise dashboards with KPI cards, variance trend charts, variance by category/type charts, heatmaps
- Analysis upload flow (enterprise-level, multi-file-set)
- Real-time streaming analysis log (WebSocket — shows agent text deltas and tool call cards as they happen)
- Results page — per-customer findings, structured finding cards with severity/category/dollar impact/recommendation
- Rollup results page
- Flash results page (customer table + top risks)
- Trend section with configurable window (1-60 months)
- Chat interface (full sidebar, message thread, tool call inline rendering, chart display, scope selector)
- Admin pages: User management, Enterprise management, Category management
- Batch status page
- History sidebar, breadcrumbs, hierarchy tree navigation

**Auth and RBAC:**
- Entra object ID-based user records
- Role assignments scoped to company, country, or enterprise
- `RoleGate` component in frontend, auth dependencies in backend

| Feature | Status |
|---------|--------|
| **Global batch upload** (one file set for all enterprises, auto-partitioned) | Planned (P0, Epic 1) — enterprise-level upload works; global partitioner is in backlog |

| **Trend pattern identification** (regional tendencies, not just charts) | TrendService exists; narrative pattern detection is backlog |

## Data Model — Key Entities

```
Company → Country → Enterprise
Enterprise → AnalysisRun (one per month, per enterprise)
AnalysisRun → VarianceRecord (one per customer)
AnalysisRun → Finding (AI-generated, one per investigation)
AnalysisRun → IssueFinding (structured, post-processed, indexed by customer + worker)
AnalysisRun → KGNode / KGEdge (knowledge graph for agent context)
AnalysisRun → FileSet (uploaded Excel files, status tracked)
AnalysisRun → intermediate tables: ForecastLineItem, RevenueActual, TimesheetEntry, NameMapping, WorkerHoursSnapshot
User → UserRoleAssignment (company/country/enterprise scoped)
ChatConversation → ChatMessage → ChatAttachment (persistent chat history)
VarianceCategoryDB (hierarchical, admin-managed, manual override on findings)
FindingNote (analyst notes on specific findings)
```

`AnalysisRun.analysis_type` distinguishes full (actuals-based) from flash (hours-only) runs.

---

## How the AI Layer Works

1. Excel files are uploaded and parsed into normalized line-item tables in the DB.
2. Aggregator joins forecast + actuals + hours at the customer level, producing `VarianceRecord` rows.
3. The duplicate allocation detector runs a deterministic pre-pass (no LLM needed for obvious duplicates).
4. `run_investigation()` fans out one `investigate_single_variance()` call per customer, up to 5 concurrent.
5. Each call: `data_gatherer` pre-fetches all relevant rows (forecast line items, timesheet entries, worker snapshots, KG context) and packs them into the prompt. Claude returns a structured finding via `tool_use`.
6. `PostProcessor` extracts `IssueFinding` records, resolves categories (from DB taxonomy or LLM output), builds customer and person issue summaries.
7. Results stream to the browser live via WebSocket — the frontend renders each agent text delta and tool call result in real time.
8. Separately, the chat interface supports ad-hoc natural language queries against a loaded analysis run — Claude uses tools to query the DB and return structured answers with charts.

---

## Current State: How Complete Is It?

**Well-built core.** The end-to-end flow — upload Excel files, run analysis, stream Claude investigation results, view findings — is production-grade. The data model is mature (18 Alembic migrations), the agent architecture is solid, and the frontend has a full UI across every major view.

**The gap is scale.** The system works per-enterprise today. The finance team's actual need is global (one upload for all 20+ offices). The global partitioner epic is the biggest remaining work item before this is operationally useful at Improving's scale.

**Contributors:** Devlin Liles (37 commits), Michael Slater (7 commits). Last commit March 4, 2026. 44 total commits, active development cadence of ~20 commits/week while in flight.
